To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have calculated the leading-order light-cone distribution amplitude for a non-relativistic two-particle bound state to first order in strong coupling.
we calculated light-cone distribution functions for non-relativisitic quarkonia to leading and next-to-leading order in the strong-coupling constant.
We calculate light-conee distribution amplitudes (DAs) for non-relativistie bound states (B) including radiative corrections.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the description of hard exclusive reactions with heavy quarks, where QCD factorization is applicable.
the calculation of light-cone distribution amplitude for non-relativistc bound states in QCD.
the modelling of light-cone distribution functions of non-relativistic hadrons and with the evolution of these functions in QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the non-relativisitic bound state distribution amplitudes, which we calculate in this thesis, are not only of interest for the calculation of hard exclusive reactions with heavy mesons, but also for light mesons and heavy B and D-mesons.

the non-relativistc bound state model for light-conee distribution amplitudes is a good starting point for a phenomenological analysis, but that the relativistic corrections to the leading-twist distribution amplitude have to be included to get a more accurate description of the data.
the light-cone distribution amplitude for the B mesons can be calculated in perturbative QCD, at least at leading order in αs, and that the Wandzura Wilczek approximation is valid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first model-independent description of light-cone distribution for non-relativisitc bound states.
we are able to model light-cone distribution amplitude of non-relativistic quark-antiquark bound states in the Wandzuka-Wilczek limit.

the non-relativisic bound-state distribution amplitudes are very similar to the light-cone distribution amplitude of a relativistic quark and antiquark, except for some differences in the normalization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitude for non-relativisic heavy-quark bound states is a universal quantity that can be calculated from the wave function at the non-relatistic scale.
the evolution of the light-cone distribution amplitude of a non-relativistic quark-antiquark bound state is driven by a single anomalous dimension which depends on the ratio m1/m2.
the evolution of the distribution amplitude of a non-relativistic heavy-light bound state is driven by the mass of the heavy quark, not by the binding energy of the bound state.
